After 1948 nearly all the Jews of the Arab world left their homes, mostly for Israel and France. About 850,000 to 900,000 people left Muslim-majority countries in the decades that followed.

Jewish communities had lived in Iraq, Yemen, Egypt, Syria and North Africa for many centuries; Baghdad's went back to the Babylonian exile. With the founding of Israel and the war of 1948, many Arab states treated Jews as enemies. Riots, arrests, loss of jobs and seizure of property followed in several countries.

  • Israel airlifted almost all of Yemen's Jews in 1949 and 1950.
  • About 120,000 Iraqi Jews left in 1950 and 1951, giving up their citizenship and goods.
  • Egypt expelled many Jews after the 1956 Suez Crisis.
  • Most Jews of Morocco, Tunisia and Algeria left in the 1950s and 1960s, many to France.

In Israel the newcomers, called Mizrahi Jews, often lived first in tent camps and faced prejudice; today their descendants make up a large share of Israelis.
